newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes flat after calm trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes flat after calm trade.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 230.00/80 per dollar, unchanged from 230-231 in early trade on a quiet interbank market, where the central bank (BNB) was the main foreign currency buyer, dealers said.
"The market was very calm and the lev closed stable as the central bank was the main buyer of dollars," a commercial bank dealer said.
A BNB official told Reuters that the bank bought and sold foreign currency but declined to specify the exchange rate or the traded volumes.
Dealers said that the BNB bought dollars near 230.80 levs for most of the day.
The lev's softening in early trade from Tuesday's close at 229-230 was due to a slight rise in dollar demand by banks and final clients in the morning.
"This could be considered normal because of the large spread between interest rates on lev-denominated and dollar-denominated investments," another dealer said.

The spread allows for a daily lev's fall against the dollar by some two levs after the BNB raised its main interest rate to 300 percent annually, effective Tuesday. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
